pages.text: Dad, in his overalls, waved a toothbrush. "Pongi, let's brush our teeth before bed." The bridge lantern was lit. It was bedtime. Pongi slipped under the blanket on the sofa. "I don't want to brush! I just want to sleep!"
Dad held the toothbrush right in front of Pongi's nose. Pongi quickly turned her head the other way. "Can't I skip it just for today?" Then she squeezed her eyes shut.
In the middle of the night, her teeth felt tickly! A bit of fish was stuck between them. A fishy smell came from her mouth. Her little brother, sleeping beside her with a shell, sniffed. "Smelly!"
Pongi opened her eyes. Dad came over. "A bit of fish is hiding between your teeth. The smell bugs are having fun all night. Let's chase them away together!" Dad took Pongi's paws in his own.
In Dad's story, white teeth stood in a row like hills. Seven round smell bugs rolled around on top, laughing. "Those are the ones that tickled me all night!" said Pongi.
"Smell bugs hate bubbles!" Dad whispered. "The toothbrush is a broom, and the foam is soap bubbles!" Dad gave Pongi the toothbrush. Pongi gripped it and jumped up.

Pongi squeezed toothpaste onto the brush. She held it in both paws and brushed up and down. Bubbles foamed up! The smell bugs ran away. Pongi thumped her tail on the floor. "Brush, brush! Goodbye, fishy smell!"
Pongi took a mouthful of water and rinsed with a gurgle. She opened wide. There was nothing between her teeth, and the smell was gone. Her little brother sniffed. "Nice!" Pongi smiled a big smile.

Pongi sang, "One, brush when the first boat passes! Two, brush again when the lantern lights up! Three, right between the teeth!" The next day, when the first boat tooted, Pongi picked up her toothbrush first.
Dad hugged Pongi tight. "Your teeth shine like fish scales!" With bubbles every night, the smell bugs couldn't come near. Pongi called, "Brush, brush! Goodbye, fishy smell!"
